title: AnswerReason
description: WHY a boundary answer is not `present` — the vocabulary a client renders when it must explain a non-answer (concern class C4; the `unverifiable` arm is C5's may-believe clause: evidence that cannot be evaluated confers nothing, in either direction). Exactly one reason (`observed_absent`) accompanies answerState `absent`; every other reason accompanies `unreachable`. A `present` answer takes no reason. Rust authority: seam_contracts::AnswerReason (crates/seam-contracts/src/answer.rs); agreement is asserted by elohim/elohim-storage/tests/schema_contract.rs.
$comment: Deliberately carries NO _dna metadata — same rationale as answer-state. `_reasonStates` is the reason-to-state pairing, declared here so a consumer with no Rust can enforce it; elohim-storage's schema_contract test asserts it agrees with AnswerReason::state(). `not_yet_delivered` is the full-arc law made speakable: on a full-arc holder a local read miss is a fact about gossip delivery, never about existence.
